title: Producer Agreement: Work for Hire and Buyout
summary: An artist or label commissions a production and owns the resulting beat and master outright, with a fee, optional points and agreed writer credit.
useWhen: The artist or label needs full ownership of the production, for example for label delivery, sync deals or catalog value.
watchOuts: Under U.S. copyright law, a work by a non-employee is a 'work made for hire' only if it falls within one of nine statutory categories (such as a contribution to a collective work or part of an audiovisual work) and the parties sign a written agreement saying so. A stand-alone sound recording or beat is often not in those categories, which is why this template also includes a written assignment.

California: commissioning a 'work made for hire' from an individual can make the commissioning party that individual's employer for workers' compensation and unemployment insurance purposes (Cal. Labor Code §3351.5(c), Unemployment Insurance Code §686). Many California deals use an assignment instead of work-for-hire language.
Composition: owning the master does not automatically give the commissioning party the producer's share of the composition. Decide whether the producer keeps their writer share or assigns it.
Authors can terminate assignments (but not true works made for hire) after 35 years under 17 U.S.C. §203. That is another reason buyers prefer valid work-for-hire status.
Interactive streams and downloads generate mechanical royalties for the composition. Make sure split sheets and registrations match the agreed composition shares.

sections.title: 1. Parties
2. Services and delivery
3. Fee
sections.body: Commissioning party will pay Producer {{fee}}, paid {{fee_schedule}}. This is the full payment for the services and rights granted, except any royalties stated below.

sections.title: 4. Ownership of masters and production
sections.body: All recordings, beats, instrumentals, stems and other results of Producer's services (the "Masters") are works made for hire for the Commissioning party to the fullest extent the law allows, as contributions to a collective work or parts of an audiovisual work where applicable. To the extent any Master is not a work made for hire, Producer assigns to the Commissioning party all rights, title and interest in it, including copyright, worldwide, for the full term of copyright and any renewals. Producer will sign further documents reasonably needed to confirm this. Producer: [[initial:producer]]

sections.title: 5. Composition: producer keeps a writer share
sections.body: Producer keeps a {{producer_comp_share}}% writer and publishing share of each composition Producer co-writes, documented in a split sheet. The Commissioning party may use the compositions in the Masters without further payment to Producer, except royalties collected through PROs, The MLC and other customary channels.

sections.title: 6. Composition: full assignment
sections.body: For the fee, Producer assigns to the Commissioning party all of Producer's rights in the musical compositions embodied in the Masters, including the writer's share of publishing income, except the writer's share of public performance income that PROs pay directly to writers, which Producer keeps where PRO rules require. Producer: [[initial:producer]]
sections.showIf: composition == 'producer assigns all composition rights for the fee'

sections.title: 7. Producer royalty
sections.body: Commissioning party will pay Producer {{points_percent}}% of its net income from exploitation of the Masters (amounts actually received, minus distribution fees), accounted twice a year within 60 days after June 30 and December 31, with statements. Producer may audit once a year.

sections.title: 8. Credit
sections.body: Commissioning party will credit Producer as "{{credit}}" in metadata and liner notes where credits appear. Producer may list the work in their portfolio after release.

sections.title: 9. Producer's promises
sections.body: Producer promises that its contribution is original, or that every sample, interpolation or third-party element in it has been disclosed in writing and is either cleared or will be cleared before release. Producer has not granted rights that conflict with this agreement. Producer will not use the Masters, or reuse the beats or stems created for them, for anyone else.

sections.title: 10. Name and likeness
sections.body: Commissioning party may use Producer's approved name, likeness and biography to promote the Masters.

sections.title: 11. California note
sections.body: California: commissioning a 'work made for hire' from an individual can make the commissioning party that individual's employer for workers' compensation and unemployment insurance purposes (Cal. Labor Code §3351.5(c), Unemployment Insurance Code §686). Many California deals use an assignment instead of work-for-hire language.

sections.title: 12. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
